uncited: **Inputs:** A set of optimized 2D surfels (position $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$, rotation $\mathbf{q}_i$, scale $\mathbf{s}_i$, opacity $o_i$, and view-dependent color parameters) and a trained multi-resolution hash grid $E_\theta$ with MLP decoder $f_\theta$.
**Outputs:** A compressed RGB texture atlas (55–320 MB for typical scenes) and the surfel attributes.
**Texture Atlas:** A 2D RGB texture where each surfel $i$ maps to a rectangular region.
The texels store the signed residual color $\rho(\mathbf{x}) = f_\theta(E_\theta(\mathbf{x}))$.
**Primitive Representation:** Represent the scene as a sparse set of oriented 2D surfels.
**Kernel Selection:** Use the Deformable Beta kernel $\mathcal{B}(x;b)$ instead of a Gaussian.
Small $b$ values produce flat, hard-edged disks to reduce overdraw; large $b$ values produce soft, Gaussian-like profiles.
*   **Hash Collisions:** Hash collisions from training can degrade quality.
*   **Sparsity:** Pipelines using per-primitive textures start from a converged dense model with densification frozen, capping sparsity.
A kernel family defined by $\mathcal{B}(x;b) = (1-x)^{\beta(b)}$ that interpolates between flat disks and soft Gaussals via the parameter $b$.
Chosen to reduce overdraw compared to standard Gaussians. [Link](1792-splat-extent-and-projection.md)
The process of converting view-independent neural queries (hash grid + MLP) into a static 2D texture map.
Enables hardware-accelerated sampling without runtime neural inference. [Link](1411-rendering-pipelines-and-passes.md)
An exact mathematical reformulation of the intersection test between a ray and a planar surfel, optimized for GPU shader performance. [Link](1792-splat-extent-and-projection.md)
*   **Time Complexity:** Rendering is dominated by texture fetches and simple arithmetic, avoiding neural network evaluations.
The rational intersection test is computationally cheaper than standard ray-surfel shaders.
*   **Strengths:** High rendering speed due to elimination of runtime neural inference; reduced overdraw via flat kernels; high sparsity.
*   **Limitations:** Larger memory footprint than some compressed 3DGS variants; requires training to bake the atlas; signed residuals require careful handling of negative values in texture formats.
*   **When to Use:** Real-time rendering of high-fidelity scenes where GPU compute is limited by neural network inference overhead.
*   **When Not to Use:** When memory is extremely constrained and smaller scene representations are prioritized over rendering speed.
It builds on 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) and FastGS, aiming to solve the rendering overhead caused by runtime neural network evaluations in neural radiance representations.
The method leverages the observation that view-independent high-frequency texture can be baked into a texture atlas, while view-dependent low-frequency appearance remains per-surfel.
